newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: KUWAIT SAYS AIMS TO BOOST UPSTREAM, DOWNSTREAM.
newsitem.headline: KUWAIT SAYS AIMS TO BOOST UPSTREAM, DOWNSTREAM.

text.p: Kuwait's Oil Minister, Isa al-Mazeedi, on Friday said the Gulf OPEC state had plans to boost its upstream and oil refining capacity.
Kuwait aimed to have a production capacity of "a little over three million barrels per day (bpd)" by the year 2005 from a current 2.4-2.5 milllion bpd, al-Mazeedi told reporters.
Refining capacity at the country's three existing plants was targeted to hit one million bpd under a four to five-year plan from the present 900,000 bpd.
Kuwait was also eyeing potential stakes in refineries in China, Thailand, India, the United States and expanding its existing downstream assets in the Netherlands and Italy.

The target for Asian refining ventures is around 200,000 bpd, though Mazeedi said this was a rough estimate as there were a number of discussions under way. He said there were also discussions with U.S. private companies, though he declined to give details.
"Right now we have nothing in the U.S. but everything is subject to negotiation," he told reporters.

In Europe, Kuwait is considering plans which include doubling the present 80,000 bpd of throughput capacity at its Rotterdam refinery and doubling capacity at its joint venture Milazzo plant with Italy's Agip SpA.
Mazeedi said that the elderly Rotterdam plant currently is operating well below capacity, at around 60-65,000 bpd.
He said the 50-50 partners in the Milazzo refinery plan to upgrade to 240-280,000 bpd.
Al-Mazeedi was speaking a day after OPEC ministers formally agreed in Vienna to roll-over the group's official output ceiling of 25.03 million bpd for the remainder of 1997.
Kuwait has an OPEC quota of two million bpd and has demanded a higher quota if the cartel increases its ceiling.
